question: Should OpenClaw add a core-owned durable `allow-always` plugin approval contract now, and should Skill Workshop opt into it before its owner, scope, and audit model are fixed?
rationale: This changes a plugin-facing API and a persistent approval security boundary, so the durable trust model and built-in Skill Workshop opt-in need maintainer intent rather than routine patch repair.

options.title: Fix scope before merge
options.body: Require a stable owner id, non-sensitive scope key, rebase-safe preservation of current approval routing, and second-call reuse proof before this PR can merge.

options.title: Land generic only
options.body: Accept the generic plugin approval API after review but remove Skill Workshop opt-in until its lifecycle approval model is separately designed.

options.title: Pause durable plugin approvals
options.body: Keep current session-only plugin approval behavior and continue tracking the broader Skill Workshop owner-approval design separately.

recommendation.title: Fix scope before merge
recommendation.body: Require a stable owner id, non-sensitive scope key, rebase-safe preservation of current approval routing, and second-call reuse proof before this PR can merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and maintained the Skill Workshop lifecycle policy that would become the built-in durable approval consumer.
